answer: A concrete Sybil defense is a per-epoch admission gate: the network admits only a bounded number of new identities each round, and each must present fresh work from a prior epoch to claim a slot. A farm cannot mint faster than the gate, so a dune of clones arrives slowly and visibly instead of all at once. Honest newcomers queue briefly, while a vault of pre-registered keys earns nothing until its turn, and a fable of instant crowd growth never materializes. The attacker's cost is time and lost races for scarce slots, which limits the rate of infiltration even with unlimited capital.
